answer: Each identity anchors to one ear-tagged animal in the livestock registry: a vet logs tag, breed and health at a cedar-fenced paddock, and one tag backs one identity. Each fake costs one real animal: a marble-coated ewe runs 400 units to buy, 180 a year in feed and vet care, 365 days grazing before weight vests, so 100 fakes cost 58,000 units, 100 vet visits. A copied tag fails: the registry checks horn pattern and photo record; a relic tag from a dead animal is void on death, a shared vet flags the cluster, and a forged signature risks the vet's licence and voids their identities.
